'''Daequan Cook''' (born April 28, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]. He was taken 21st overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] then subsequently traded to the [[Miami Heat]].

==High school career==
Daequan Cook attended [[Dunbar High School (Ohio)|Paul Laurence Dunbar High School]] in [[Dayton, Ohio]]. As a junior, he led Dunbar to the Ohio Division II state semifinals where they lost to eventual champion Upper Sandusky High School. As a senior, he averaged 24.9 points, 6.0 rebounds and 5.0 assists per game and led Dunbar to a Division II state championship. He was named onto the 2006 [[McDonald's All-American Team]]. Playing for the West, Cook scored 17 points in the 112–94 win.<ref name="draftprofile">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/DaequanCook.html|title=NBA.com: Daequan Cook Draft 2007 Profile|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> He was also named a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].

Cook was a high school teammate of [[Norris Cole (basketball)|Norris Cole]]. (The two later faced each other in the [[2012 NBA Finals]].)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/fl-xpm-2012-06-17-fl-miami-heat-news-0618-20120617-story.html|title=Former teammates Norris Cole and Daequan Cook square off in NBA Finals|first=Shandel Richardson, Sun|last=Sentinel|website=Sun-Sentinel.com}}</ref> Cook also played with [[Mark Titus]], [[Greg Oden]] and [[Mike Conley Jr.]] on the SPIECE Indy Heat high school [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team. Cook was the team's leading scorer in the 2004 Big Time event in [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]]. The team was undefeated and won the championship.

==College career==
One of [[Ohio State University]] Coach [[Thad Matta]]'s famed "Thad Five", Cook averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 0.7 steals in 20.4 minutes per game. On April 20, 2007, Cook announced his intentions to enter the [[2007 NBA draft]], along with fellow freshmen teammates [[Greg Oden]] and [[Mike Conley Jr.]]

==Professional career==

===NBA===
[[File:Omer Asik blockshot.jpg|200px|thumbnail|right|Cook in pre-season game versus [[Houston Rockets]] in 2012]]

====Miami Heat (2007–2010)====
Daequan Cook was averaging 8.2 points per game in his rookie season with the [[Miami Heat]] before being sent to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the NBA D-League in late February 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/daequancookjoelanthonyiowahtml|title=Daequan Cook and Joel Anthony Assigned to Iowa Energy|website=Miami Heat}}</ref> He returned to the Heat on March 8<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/cook_anthony_recall.html|title=HEAT Recall Daequan Cook and Joel Anthony From NBA D-League|website=Miami Heat}}</ref> and in his second game back on March 10 he scored a career-high 23 points in a one-point loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers|L.A. Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280310014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209183534/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280310014|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 9, 2019|title=Clippers vs. Heat - Game Recap - March 10, 2008 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He scored a new career-high of 27 against the [[Phoenix Suns]] on March 4, 2009, going 6–8 from 3-point range.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290304014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825193029/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290304014|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 25, 2016|title=Suns vs. Heat - Game Recap - March 4, 2009 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Cook won the [[2008–09 NBA season|2009]] [[NBA All-Star Weekend Three-Point Shootout]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], ending [[Jason Kapono]]'s two-year winning streak.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2009/news/story?id=3908104|title=Knicks' Robinson stuffs Howard for dunk crown|date=February 15, 2009|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

====Oklahoma City Thunder (2010–2012)====
On June 23, 2010, Cook was traded with the 18th pick in the [[2010 NBA draft|2010 draft]] to the Oklahoma City Thunder for the 32nd pick in the 2010 Draft.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/trade_release100623.html |title=Thunder Acquires 18th Pick and Daequan Cook from Heat |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-06-23 |access-date=2010-06-24}}</ref>

In 2010–2011, Cook emerged as a useful bench player for the Thunder, mostly as a three-point specialist. He was a key player in the Thunder's emergence as a Western Conference contender. In December 2011, Cook signed a two-year extension with the Thunder. Cook reached the 2012 NBA Finals with the Thunder, but the team lost to the Miami Heat.

====Houston Rockets (2012–2013)====
On October 27, 2012, Cook, [[James Harden]], [[Cole Aldrich]], and [[Lazar Hayward]] were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Kevin Martin (basketball, born 1983)|Kevin Martin]], [[Jeremy Lamb]], and draft picks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/27/james-harden-traded-to-rockets.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpts |title=Cook traded to Rockets |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130804033515/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/27/james-harden-traded-to-rockets.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpts |archive-date=2013-08-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cook was waived by the Rockets on January 2, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11911 |title=Houston Rockets sign James Anderson, release Daequan Cook |access-date=2013-01-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202224142/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11911 |archive-date=2013-12-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====Chicago Bulls (2013)====
On January 6, 2013, Cook signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agent-guard-daequan-cook.html|title=Bulls sign free agent guard Daequan Cook|website=Chicago Bulls}}</ref> and played there for the remainder of the season.

===Overseas===

====Budivelnyk / Tübingen (2013–2014)====
On November 23, 2013, Cook has signed his first overseas contract, with [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague|Ukrainian SuperLeague]] team [[Budivelnyk Kyiv]], which also participating in the [[Euroleague Basketball|Euroleague]].<ref>{{cite web|script-title=uk:Декван Кук стал игроком "Будивельника"! |url=http://budivelnyk.ua/news/1363-dekvan-kuk-stal-igrokom-budivelnika |publisher=budivelnyk.ua |language=uk |access-date=25 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202222953/http://budivelnyk.ua/news/1363-dekvan-kuk-stal-igrokom-budivelnika |archive-date=2 December 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=BUDIVELNIK KIEV tabs three-point specialist Cook|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/124344/8177/budivelnik-kiev-tabs-three-point-specialist-cook|access-date=August 12, 2014|work=Euroleague.net}}</ref> In his Euroleague debut, Cook scored 16 points with 4/8 from 3-point range in his team loss 74–82 to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Budivelnyk Kiev 74 - 82 CSKA Moscow|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=74&pcode=005319&seasoncode=E2013#!boxscore|access-date=29 November 2013|newspaper=euroleague.net}}</ref> Budivelnyk waived him on January 14, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Daequan Cook waived by Budivelnyk|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/71615/daequan-cook-waived-by-budivelnyk.html|access-date=14 January 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref> On January 29, 2014, he signed with [[Walter Tigers Tübingen]] of Germany for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kaum zu glauben! Ex-NBA-Profi Daequan Cook wird ein Tiger|url=http://walter-tigers.de/index.php?id=63&tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=1877&cHash=ce139d79acd7faa5938498b38a400238|publisher=walter-tigers.de|language=de|access-date=30 January 2014}}</ref>

====SPO Rouen (2014–2015)====
On August 12, 2014, Cook signed with [[SPO Rouen Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Un NBAer au SPO Rouen!|url=http://www.basketsporouenkinder.com/Actualite-3496-un-nbaer-au-spo-rouen|language=fr|access-date=August 12, 2014|work=basketsporouenkinder.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140813083742/http://www.basketsporouenkinder.com/Actualite-3496-un-nbaer-au-spo-rouen|archive-date=August 13, 2014}}</ref>

====Benfica (2015–2016)====
On August 14, 2015, Cook signed with Portuguese champions [[S.L. Benfica (basketball)|S.L. Benfica]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slbenfica.pt/noticias/detalhedenoticia/tabid/2788/ArticleId/42650/language/pt-PT/.aspx |title=Podem contar com o meu melhor |language=pt |trans-title=You can count with my best |date=14 August 2015 |publisher=[[S.L. Benfica]] |access-date=14 August 2015}}</ref> On March 13, 2016, Cook recorded a career-high 44 points, while shooting 15-of-32 from the field, along with nine rebounds and three assists in a 94–97 loss to [[FC Porto (basketball)|Porto]].<ref>{{cite news | title=SL Benfica 94 at FC Porto Ferpinta 97 | url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-03-13/SL-Benfica-at-FC-Porto-Ferpinta/235953 | date=March 13, 2016 | work=RealGM.com| access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref>

====Chemidor Tehran (2016–2017)====
In December 2016, Cook signed with [[Chemidor Tehran BC|Chemidor Tehran]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/news/472016/Daequan-Cook-(ex-Benfica)-joins-Chemidor|title=Asia-Basket|website=www.asia-basket.com}}</ref>

====Ironi Nes Ziona (2017–2020)====
[[File:Daequan Cook 2019.jpg|200px|thumbnail|right|Cook with Ironi Nes Ziona in March 2019]]
On August 9, 2017, Cook signed with the Israeli team [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/243827/daequan-cook-inks-with-ironi-nes-ziona.html|title=Daequan Cook inks with Ironi Nes-Ziona|date=August 9, 2017|work=Sportando.com|access-date=August 9, 2017}}</ref> In 32 games played during the 2017–18 season, he led the team in scoring by averaging 16 points per game. Cook led Nes Ziona to the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Play-offs|2018 Israeli League Playoffs]], where they eventually lost to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the Quarterfinals.

On June 7, 2018, Cook signed a one-year contract extension with Nes Ziona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/276295/ironi-nes-ziona-re-signs-daequan-cook.html|title=Ironi Nes-Ziona re-signs Daequan Cook|date=June 7, 2018|work=Sportando.com|access-date=June 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143500/https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/276295/ironi-nes-ziona-re-signs-daequan-cook.html|archive-date=June 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 9, 2018, Cook recorded 24 points, shooting 5-of-8 from three-point range, including a game-winning three-point shot with 2.9 seconds left to give Nes Ziona an 83–81 win over [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. He was subsequently named [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 9 MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|title=מצטיין המחזור התשיעי: דקוואן קוק|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19632|access-date=December 11, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=December 11, 2018|language=he}}</ref> On April 7, 2019, Cook recorded a season-high 30 points, shooting 7-of-11 from three-point range, along with three assists, leading Nes Ziona to a 97–84 win over [[Hapoel Holon]]. He was subsequently named [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 25 MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-25: דקוואן קוק|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=21064|access-date=April 9, 2019|work=basket.co.il|date=April 9, 2019|language=he}}</ref>

On August 1, 2019, Cook signed a one-year contract extension with Nes Ziona.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=21451|title=מרגיש בבית: קוק ממשיך בלב המושבה|date=August 1, 2019|work=basket.co.il|access-date=August 1, 2019|language=he}}</ref> On December 1, 2019, Cook recorded a season-high 34 points, while shooting 13-of-24 from the field, along with seven rebounds and two assists in a 106–115 double overtime loss to [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]].<ref>{{cite news | title=Winner League, Game 8: Nes Ziona Vs Gilboa Galil | url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24065&lang=en | date=December 1, 2019 | work=basket.co.il | access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref>

On August 24, 2020, Cook signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hapoel Tel Aviv tabs Daequan Cook |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-tel-aviv-tabs-daequan-cook/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 24, 2020 |date=August 24, 2020}}</ref> However, his contract was voided on September 6 and the team replaced him with [[Jon Diebler]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Deal between Hapoel Tel Aviv, Daequan Cook voided |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/deal-between-hapoel-tel-aviv-daequan-cook-voided/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 6, 2020 |date=September 6, 2020}}</ref>
